cause: Context Pack was frozen before development started.
impact: The line has an evidence-bound starting context.
lesson: Freeze the initial context before changing implementation state.

cause: RunForm renders family controls through hard-coded comparisons -- modelType === 'iv_2sls', 'did', 'cs_did', 'sa_did', 'dcdh', 'panel_ols', 'linear_mixed_effects', 'time_series.arma_garch' -- and V186ModelControls carries a literal family list plus a switch over default options.
impact: This is the enumeration matrix that blocks 2 and 3 removed from the design layer and P0 removed from the agent projection, still standing on the frontend. Adding a family costs a branch here even though the backend now costs only declarations, so the frontend is where the per-family cost has concentrated.
lesson: Removing an enumeration from one layer does not remove it from the system. The capability projection already publishes what the form needs to derive its rendering, so the material for a capability-driven form exists; converting it is a scope of its own rather than something to fold into adding an entry point.

cause: The complex survey design declarations and the ANOVA options now have controls in RunForm and travel with the run through api.ts.
impact: Frontend 190 files / 1643 tests passed against 188 / 1634, tsc clean. Both capabilities were reachable only through the API or CLI before this.
lesson: The replicate types and single-PSU policies are read from /capabilities rather than restated in the form, and a test narrows the published sets and asserts the options follow -- a local copy would pass every test while disagreeing with what the engine accepts. The sums-of-squares selector starts empty for the same reason the backend refuses an undeclared type: a pre-selected default in the form would make the refusal unreachable and hand the user a choice they never made.

cause: The survey design and ANOVA controls were wired into RunForm. The entry point a user reaches from 'Import data and create analysis' is GenesisWizard, which imports the same controls, holds the same capabilities hook and is structurally near-identical, so the mistake was invisible in the source.
impact: Component tests, RunForm tests and the whole frontend suite passed -- 190 files, 1643 tests green -- while the controls rendered nowhere in the running product. Only opening the application in a browser showed the form had no survey group at all.
lesson: v1.8.6 shipped functions nothing called; this is the same failure one level up -- a form wired correctly that nobody opens. No test could have caught it: the component tests test the component, the RunForm tests test RunForm, and both were right about the wrong path. Where two components can serve the same purpose, the test has to name the one the product actually routes to, which is why the reachability assertions now live in the GenesisWizard suite.

cause: The survey design engine names the intercept `(Intercept)` to match R; the result payload has named it `Intercept` since long before this version. The merge in _apply_survey_design_variance skipped terms it could not match, so the intercept kept the naive HC1 standard error while every slope received the design one.
impact: A browser run on the committed survey fixture returned intercept SE 0.7804 against R svyglm's 1.5955 -- half the true width -- displayed beside x1 and x2 matching R to twelve decimals, with no field distinguishing them. Every backend and frontend test passed: the engine suites drive estimate_with_design directly and never walk a run's coefficient table.
lesson: Asserting on the interesting coefficients is not asserting on the result. The oracle comparisons all targeted slopes, so a whole term could carry the wrong variance undetected. A merge keyed on names must fail loudly on an unmatched key -- silently leaving the previous value is indistinguishable from success and produces a number the user cannot tell apart from a correct one.

cause: `model.rerun` carries two schemas: `editable_schema`, which describes the operation, and `proposal_schema`, which is what reaches the language model. Opening the survey fields touched only the first, plus the validator. The tool contract the model is handed still declared `properties: {model_options}` with `additionalProperties: false`.
impact: Backend suites, the capability projection and a real rerun through HTTP all passed while the Agent remained unable to emit the fields at all -- the tool schema forbade them. A test asserting schema/validator agreement passed too, because it read `editable_schema`. Separately, `sampling_weight` had never been published as a family param since v1.8.6, so no rerun could change any weight either.
lesson: The same shape as the RunForm/GenesisWizard defect one layer down: two near-identical artifacts, and the one that was verified is not the one the product consumes. When a contract exists in more than one form, the test has to name the copy the real consumer reads -- here the LLM -- and the fix is to generate both from a single declaration rather than to keep them in step.
